reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly: same three order IDs and amounts. Next I'll list the orders to see which customers are in this batch.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly, so the refund work checks out. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 48125 matches my check: orders 210 and 213 total 63258, less refund 213 of 15133. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 54597 matches my check: orders 211 and 214 total 73966, less refunds 211 and 214 totaling 19369. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
All three net balances match my independent check against the orders and the ledger's refunds, so Alpha's refund work looks complete. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 54597 matches my check (orders 211 and 214 total 73966, less refunds 12701 and 6668). Recording birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 46961 matches my check: orders 212 and 215 total 46961, and cobalt has no refunds. Acme and birch are already paid, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each amount matches my independent check against the orders and the ledger's refunds, so the batch is complete.
